source_text:
Ἰσαὰκ ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον
συνεποδίζετο καὶ ἀμνὸς ἀντ' αὐτοῦ ἐσφάζετο, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ σταυροῦ ἀνεφέρετο καὶ τῇ σαρκὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐσταυροῦτο καὶ πάσχουσα ἡ σὰρξ ἡ θεότης οὐκ ἔπασχεν. Ἔστη τὸ ἱστίον τοῦ σταυροῦ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ τοῦ κόσμου καὶ ὁ κόσμος ἀναυάγητος ἔμεινεν· τούτῳ τῷ ἱστίῳ τοῦ σταυροῦ ὁ πλέων ναυάγιον θανάτου οὐκ οἶδεν, ἀλλὰ εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀναπλέει. Οὐκέτι Εὔα φοβεῖται τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν τοῦ Ἀδάμ, ἐν γὰρ Μαρίᾳ τὸ ταύτης πταῖσμα ἀνασέσωσται· οὐκέτι Ἀδὰμ φοβεῖται τὸν ὄφιν, Χριστὸς γὰρ συνέτριψεν τὴν κεφαλὴν τοῦ δράκοντος· Σὺ γάρ, φησίν, συνέτριψας τὴν κεφαλὴν τοῦ δράκοντος ἐπὶ τοῦ ὕδατος, τουτέστιν ἐπὶ τοῦ βαπτίσματος. Οὐκέτι πενθῶ, οὐκέτι κλαίω λέγων· Ἐστράφην εἰς ταλαιπωρίαν ἐν τῷ ἐμπαγῆναί μοι ἄκανθαν· ἐλθὼν γὰρ ὁ Χριστὸς τὴν ἄκανθαν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν ἐκριζώσας τῇ ἑαυτοῦ κεφαλῇ ἐπέθηκεν. Λέλυταί μου ἡ ἀρχαία λύπη, λέλυται ἡ παλαιὰ ἀρὰ ἡ λέγουσα· Ἀκάνθας καὶ τριβόλους ἀνατελεῖ σοι ἡ γῆ· ἐξηράνθησαν γὰρ αἱ ἄκανθαι, ἐξεριζώθη ὁ τρίβολος καὶ τρίπλοκος στέφανος τῇ κεφαλῇ μου ἐπετέθη. Τίς Ἰουδαίων καὶ Ἑλλήνων πιστεύει ὅτι ξύλον ἔστη καὶ ζωὴν ἐξήνθησεν; καὶ καθ' ἑκάστην ἡμέραν ὑπὸ πιστῶν τρυγᾶται καὶ ὁ καρπὸς ἀδαπάνητος μένει· καὶ πᾶσα φυλὴ καὶ πᾶν ἔθνος πιστῶν ἐπὶ τοῦτο τὸ δένδρον βήματι ψυχῆς ἀναβαίνει καὶ τὸν κόλπον τῆς διανοίας ἀθανάτου καρποῦ πληροῖ, καὶ πάντας βαστάζει τὸ δένδρον καὶ πάντας χορτάζει καὶ σφραγίζει καὶ πλουτίζει καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀκοντίζει. Τί γὰρ δι' ἡμᾶς οὐχ ὑπέμεινεν κληθῆναι Χριστός; Οὐ δυνάμεθα ἐξαριθμήσασθαι αὐτοῦ τὰ ὀνόματα, ἐπιχείρω δὲ λέγειν, ἀγαπητοί· θύρα, ὁδός, πρόβατον, ποιμήν, σκώληξ, λίθος, μαργαρίτης, ἄνθος, ἄγγελος, ἄνθρωπος, θεός, φῶς, πηγή, ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης. Ὁ πολυώνυμος Χριστὸς καὶ εἷς ὑπάρχων, πολυώνυμος ὁ υἱὸς καὶ εἷς ὢν οὐ τρεπόμενος, οὐ μεταβαλλόμενος, ἄτρεπτος γὰρ ἡ θεότης· ἀλλ' ἑκάστῳ πράγματι κατὰ τὴν ἐνέργειαν ἁρμοζόμενος ἴδιον ὄνομα ἑκάστῃ ἐνεργείᾳ τεθεικώς. Καὶ ἴδωμεν, ἀγαπητοί, εἰ δυνάμεθα ἑκάστῳ ὀνόματι τὴν ἐνέργειαν παραστῆσαι. Ὁδὸς ἤκουσεν· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι, φησίν, ἡ ὁδὸς καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια, ἐπειδὴ αὐτὸς ἀρχηγὸς πασῶν τῶν ἀρετῶν καὶ τῆς εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀναβάσεως γέγονεν. Ὁ αὐτὸς θύρα· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι ἡ θύρα τῶν προβάτων, ἐπειδὴ δι' αὐτοῦ καθάπερ διὰ θύρας εἰς τὴν τῶν οὐρανῶν βασιλείαν εἰσερχόμεθα. Ἅλας ἤκουσεν, ἐπειδὴ τὴν δυσωδίαν τῆς εἰδωλολατρείας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπέσμηξεν καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν πρὸς νοστὸν εὐσεβείας τῇ πίστει ἤρτυσεν καὶ τὰ λελυμένα μέλη τῆς διανοίας τῇ ἀληθείᾳ συνέσφιγξεν.
thought_title: The Cross as the World's Sail and the Many Names of Christ
orientation: Amphilochius is preaching to the congregation about the newly baptized, and has just described the cross as a bridal chamber; now he moves from the type of Isaac to the cross as the world's sail and begins listing the many names of Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Isaac to the altar was being bound [by the feet] and a lamb in place of him was being slain, and the Son of God upon a cross was being offered up and in the flesh for us was being crucified and suffering the flesh the divinity was not suffering. Stood the sail of the cross in the ship of the world and the world unshipwrecked remained; with this sail of the cross the one sailing shipwreck of death does not know, but into heavens sails up. No longer Eve fears the reproach of Adam, for in Mary her fault has been saved; no longer Adam fears the serpent, for Christ crushed the head of the dragon; You for, he says, crushed the head of the dragon upon the water, that is upon baptism. No longer I mourn, no longer I weep saying: I was turned into misery when was stuck in me a thorn; for having come Christ the thorn of our sins having uprooted upon his own head placed [it]. Has been loosed my ancient grief, has been loosed the old curse that says: Thorns and thistles will sprout to you the earth; for were dried up the thorns, was uprooted the thistle and a triple-woven crown upon my head was placed. Who of Jews and Greeks believes that wood stood and life blossomed? and each day by the faithful it is harvested and the fruit unspent remains; and every tribe and every nation of the faithful upon this tree with step of soul goes up and the bosom of the mind with immortal fruit fills, and all bears the tree and all feeds and seals and enriches and after these things into heavens hurls. What for for us did he not endure to be called Christ? We are not able to count out his names, I attempt but to speak, beloved; door, way, sheep, shepherd, worm, stone, pearl, flower, angel, man, God, light, spring, sun of righteousness. The many-named Christ and one being, many-named the Son and one being not turning, not changing, for unchangeable [is] the divinity; but to each matter according to the working fitting himself a proper name to each working having set. And let us see, beloved, if we are able to each name the working to present. Way he was called; I for am, he says, the way and the truth, since he himself leader of all the virtues and of the into heavens ascent has become. The same door; I for am the door of the sheep, since through him just as through a door into the kingdom of the heavens we enter. Salt he was called, since the stench of the idolatry of men he wiped away and our souls toward the savor of piety with faith he seasoned and the loosened limbs of the mind with truth he bound together.

lemmas.gloss: was being bound by the feet

choices.english: was being bound by the feet
choices.why: The compound verb means binding the feet together, which fits the type of Isaac being prepared for sacrifice; 'bound' alone loses the specific foot-binding image.
The alpha-privative adjective is a striking coinage; keeping the negative prefix preserves the rhetorical force that the world did not suffer shipwreck.
The perfect tense indicates a completed state of salvation for Eve's fault in Mary; 'has been saved' keeps the perfect force.
The adjective describes the crown of thorns as woven of three strands, a vivid image of the passion; 'triple-woven' preserves the compound.
The alpha-privative means the fruit is not used up or consumed despite daily harvesting; 'unspent' captures the inexhaustibility.
The verb means to throw like a javelin; 'hurls' conveys the forceful sending of the faithful into heaven, stronger than 'sends'.

pass_b_english: Isaac was being bound by the feet on the altar, and a lamb was being slaughtered in his place; and the Son of God was being carried up on the cross and was being crucified in the flesh for us, and while the flesh was suffering, the divinity was not suffering. The sail of the cross stood in the ship of the world, and the world remained unshipwrecked; the one who sails with this sail of the cross knows no shipwreck of death, but sails up into the heavens. Eve no longer fears the reproach of Adam, for in Mary her fault has been saved; Adam no longer fears the serpent, for Christ crushed the head of the dragon. For you, he says, crushed the head of the dragon upon the water, that is, upon baptism. I no longer mourn, I no longer weep saying: I was turned to misery when a thorn was stuck in me; for Christ came, uprooted the thorn of our sins, and placed it on his own head. My ancient grief is loosed, the old curse is loosed that says: Thorns and thistles the earth shall bring forth for you; for the thorns are dried up, the thistle is uprooted, and a triple-woven crown has been placed on my head. Who among Jews and Greeks believes that wood stood and life blossomed? And every day it is harvested by the faithful, and the fruit remains unspent; and every tribe and every nation of the faithful climbs this tree with the step of the soul and fills the bosom of the mind with immortal fruit, and the tree carries all and feeds all and seals all and enriches all, and after these things hurls them into the heavens. For what did Christ not endure on our account, that he should be called Christ? We cannot count his names, but I attempt to speak, beloved: door, way, sheep, shepherd, worm, stone, pearl, flower, angel, man, God, light, spring, sun of righteousness. The many-named Christ is also one; the many-named Son is also one, not turning, not changing, for the divinity is unchanging; but fitting himself to each matter according to the working, he has set a proper name for each working. And let us see, beloved, if we can present the working for each name. He was called way: For I am, he says, the way and the truth, because he himself became the leader of all the virtues and of the ascent into the heavens. The same one is door: For I am the door of the sheep, because through him, as through a door, we enter into the kingdom of the heavens. He was called salt, because he wiped away the stench of idolatry from human beings and seasoned our souls with faith for the return to piety and bound together the loosened limbs of the mind with truth.

problems.quote: For what did Christ not endure to be called for us?
problems.source_quote: Τί γὰρ δι' ἡμᾶς οὐχ ὑπέμεινεν κληθῆναι Χριστός;
problems.why: κληθῆναι Χριστός means 'to be called Christ/anointed', not 'to be called for us'; δι' ἡμᾶς goes with ὑπέμεινεν
problems.fix: For what did Christ not endure on our account, that he should be called Christ?
problems.ruling: κληθῆναι Χριστός = 'to be called Christ'; English 'to be called for us' misreads δι' ἡμᾶς with κληθῆναι, changing meaning.

problems.why: νόστος means 'return/homecoming', not 'sweetness'; the phrase means 'return to piety/devotion'
problems.fix: seasoned our souls with faith for the return to piety
problems.ruling: νόστος = 'return/homecoming', not 'sweetness'; 'sweetness of piety' mistranslates νόστον εὐσεβείας, changing meaning.

edits.old: For what did Christ not endure to be called for us?
edits.new: For what did Christ not endure on our account, that he should be called Christ?

edits.old: seasoned our souls with faith toward the sweetness of piety
edits.new: seasoned our souls with faith for the return to piety

fixed: κληθῆναι Χριστός means 'to be called Christ', and δι' ἡμᾶς modifies ὑπέμεινεν, so the English misstated the source; corrected.
νόστον εὐσεβείας means 'return to piety', not 'sweetness of piety'; corrected.

last_rejected.quote: Isaac was being bound by the feet
last_rejected.why: συνεποδίζετο means feet were tied/bound together, not 'by the feet' as agency; 'bound hand and foot' or 'had his feet bound'
last_rejected.fix: Isaac had his feet bound on the altar
last_rejected.ruling: συνεποδίζετο = 'bound by the feet'; English conveys feet were bound, not agency. Acceptable rendering.

last_rejected.why: ἀνασέσωσται is passive 'has been healed/cured,' not 'saved'; 'fault' is healed, not saved
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνασέσωσται = 'saved/rescued'; 'saved' is within normal range. Not a major error.

last_rejected.why: The English hides that Christ is speaking (quoting Psalm 73/74 LXX); 'he says' should mark Christ's voice clearly
last_rejected.ruling: φησί = 'he says'; English preserves this. Identifying the specific speaker is interpretation, not translation error.

last_rejected.quote: I was turned to misery when a thorn was stuck in me
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐστράφην εἰς ταλαιπωρίαν ἐν τῷ ἐμπαγῆναί μοι ἄκανθαν
last_rejected.why: ἐμπαγῆναι means 'fixed/implanted,' not 'stuck in me' as accidental; 'when a thorn was planted in me' or 'fixed upon me'
last_rejected.fix: I was turned to misery when a thorn was fixed upon me
last_rejected.ruling: ἐμπαγῆναι = 'fixed/stuck'; 'stuck in me' conveys the meaning adequately. Minor preference only.

last_rejected.quote: placed it on his own head
last_rejected.why: The thorn is the crown of thorns; 'placed it' loses that Christ took the curse upon himself; 'wore it' or 'bore it'
last_rejected.fix: and set it on his own head
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπέθηκεν = 'placed on'; 'placed it on his own head' is accurate. 'Wore/bore' is preference, not error.

last_rejected.why: τρίβολος is 'thistle' but contextually the triple-thorn curse; better 'the thistle too is uprooted'
last_rejected.fix: the thistle is uprooted as well
last_rejected.ruling: τρίβολος = 'thistle'; 'thistle is uprooted' is correct. Adding 'too' is stylistic preference.

last_rejected.why: ἀκοντίζει means 'launches/throws like a javelin,' but 'hurls' suggests violence; 'shoots them up to' or 'launches them into'
last_rejected.ruling: ἀκοντίζει = 'hurls/throws'; 'hurls' is within normal range. Connotation nuance is preference, not error.

last_rejected.quote: For what did Christ not endure on our account, that he should be called Christ?
last_rejected.source_quote: Τί γὰρ δι' ἡμᾶς οὐχ ὑπέμεινεν κληθῆναι Χριστός;
last_rejected.why: κληθῆναι Χριστός is passive 'to be called Christ,' but the sense is 'what name did he not endure to be called for us?'
last_rejected.fix: For what name did he not endure to be called for our sake?
last_rejected.ruling: κληθῆναι Χριστός = 'to be called Christ'; English is literal and accurate. Context clarifies meaning.

last_rejected.why: The mustard seed (κόκκος σινάπεως) in the source list is completely omitted from the English; the list jumps from 'sun of righteousness' but actually the source has it before—wait, checking: source has θύρα, ὁδός, πρόβατον, ποιμήν, σκώληξ, λίθος, μαργαρίτης, ἄνθος, ἄγγελος, ἄνθρωπος, θεός, φῶς, πηγή, ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης. No mustard seed in this section! The glossary entry is for the work, not this section. No omission.
last_rejected.ruling: No κόκος σινάπεως in source list; claimant self-corrected. No omission exists.

last_rejected.quote: seasoned our souls with faith for the return to piety
last_rejected.source_quote: τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν πρὸς νοστὸν εὐσεβείας τῇ πίστει ἤρτυσεν
last_rejected.why: πρὸς νοστὸν εὐσεβείας is 'for the return to piety,' but νοστός is 'return home/homecoming'; 'homecoming to piety' or 'return to devotion'
last_rejected.fix: seasoned our souls with faith for the homecoming to piety
last_rejected.ruling: νοστὸν = 'return'; 'return to piety' is valid. 'Homecoming' nuance is preference, not major error.
